findings_to_judge.finding: The market paid +12.84% in one session (close 339.31 on 26 Aug to 382.85 on 27 Aug 2026) for nothing but a StreetInsider rumour that PANW is circling Cribl ($3.5bn) and ClickHouse ($15bn) - yet every time PANW has actually announced a deal the stock has been sold: -14% over two days on the CyberArk announcement (30 Jul 2025) and -7.42% the session after the 19 Nov 2025 print at which Chronosphere was announced alongside a double beat.

Tonight's first-ever FY27 EPS guide has to be built on roughly 9-10% more shares than the FY26 base: PANW's own Q3 FY26 release guides FY26 diluted shares to 763-766m but Q4 alone to 830-840m, and PANW has already cut its own FY26 EPS guide once on this exact mechanism (from $3.80-3.90 to $3.65-3.70 on 17 Feb 2026, on deal costs that more than doubled), a print after which the stock closed -6.82%.

PANW's GSA OneGov agreement gives every federal agency up to 60% off list on designated bundles of Prisma AIRS Runtime Security, VM-Series software firewalls, Panorama/CDSS, Prisma SASE and Prisma Browser (35% on Code to Cloud) through 31 Jan 2028 - and PANW's fiscal Q1 FY27, the quarter it guides tonight, is the first US federal year-end (30 Sep) buying quarter to run entirely under that pricing.
